**Date:** 2026-08-17 · **Tag:** `v5.2.0` · **Baseline:** `v5.1.0` · Minor release

Install: `aztec-up install 5.2.0` · Docker: `aztecprotocol/aztec:5.2.0`

## Summary

A maintenance release focused on running nodes: prover nodes use much less memory, epoch proving recovers from faults instead of giving up, p2p and mempool handling is hardened, and several L1 interactions stop wasting gas and RPC calls. Contract developers get a new Noir compiler with one breaking change (a one-line fix per note type). Wallets and PXE get faster sync with no API changes.

Protocol constants are unchanged, so v5.1.0 and v5.2.0 nodes interoperate. Upgrading needs no coordination, no downtime window, and no contract redeployment.

## Should you upgrade?

- **Node operators — recommended.** Not strictly required, but this release carries substantial p2p hardening and prover reliability and memory improvements. It is drop-in against the current rollup: upgrade the image and restart, in any order across your fleet.
- **Contract developers — upgrade when ready; one breaking change when you do.** Contracts built with v5.1.0 keep working. When you move to the v5.2.0 toolchain, note types declared inside a `contract` block need `pub` — see below.
- **Wallet / PXE developers — a plain version bump.** No breaking API changes, and sync gets faster.

## Breaking changes

- **`[Aztec.nr]` Note types declared inside a contract must be `pub`** — the new Noir compiler enforces visibility more strictly. If a `#[note]` struct is declared directly inside your `contract` block without `pub`, compilation fails with ``Function `get_id` is private``. Add `pub`; that's the whole fix. Notes declared in their own module are already `pub` and unaffected ([#24907](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/24907)).

  ```diff
    #[derive(Packable, Eq)]
    #[note]
  - struct MyNote {
  + pub struct MyNote {
        owner: AztecAddress,
    }
  ```

## For contract developers

- **Noir compiler: `v1.0.0-beta.22` → `v1.0.0-beta.25`** ([#24907](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/24907)). Besides the `pub` change above, Noir itself removed some long-deprecated stdlib items (the `as_slice` methods and the `std::hash::keccak` module) and reports previously-silent ambiguous method calls as errors. If your contract used none of these, it compiles as before.
- **The `getTxEffects` oracle now works** — reading an element of the array it returns previously failed to compile, because `TxEffect` did not implement `Deserialize`. It now does ([#25109](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25109)).

## For node operators

The bulk of the release. There are no consensus or protocol changes: v5.1.0 and v5.2.0 nodes interoperate, so roll your fleet at your own pace.

**Prover nodes**

- **Much lower memory use.** The prover stack kept large data in memory long after it was needed — every checkpoint's transactions, circuit inputs, and proofs, some of it duplicating what was already on disk; one duplication alone accounted for ~7.6 GiB in a 5 TPS test. This data is now released promptly and read back from disk when needed ([#24982](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/24982), [#24983](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/24983), [#24990](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/24990), [#25027](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25027)).
- **Epoch proving retries instead of giving up.** An epoch is declared failed only when its submission window expires, not on the first fault; a chain prune during proving no longer counts as a failure; and stuck epochs aren't pointlessly re-proved. Diagnostics for each failed checkpoint are uploaded as they happen ([#24678](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/24678)).

**Mempool and p2p**

- **Incoming gossiped transactions are no longer held up** by the pool's background archiving work ([#25148](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25148)).
- **A node whose p2p service fails to start now exits at startup** instead of running in a broken state ([#25177](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25177)). While a node has zero peers it warns periodically ([#25183](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25183)) and holds off proposing, slash voting, and accepting transactions until it reconnects ([#25185](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25185)).

**L1**

- **Event watching switched from `eth_newFilter` to polling `getLogs`.** Server-side filters break behind load-balanced RPC providers — nodes were re-polling dead filters at 30–40 req/s and silently missing slashing and governance events ([#25176](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25176)).
- **A stale governance payload setting no longer wastes gas.** A sequencer left with an outdated `GOVERNANCE_PROPOSER_PAYLOAD` kept signalling a payload that had already executed, burning ~100k gas per slot. It now detects this and stops ([#24764](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/24764)).
- **Spurious "insufficient funds" errors when simulating L1 calls are fixed** ([#25202](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25202)).
- **The KZG trusted setup loads at startup** rather than stalling the first blob operation ([#24775](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/24775)).

**Validators and sync**

- **You are warned when the network votes to slash your validators.** The node now logs warnings and exposes metrics when its own validators appear as slash targets — previously operators found out only after stake was lost ([#25058](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25058)).
- **Block proposals containing invalid transactions are correctly flagged as slashable.** An error in transaction validation previously let such proposers escape accountability ([#25031](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25031)).
- **A sync race causing spurious `block_not_available` errors is fixed** ([#25206](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25206)).
- **Reorged blocks are fully cleaned from the archiver**, including blocks whose transactions were re-included elsewhere ([#24765](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/24765)); a related race when reading L2→L1 message proofs is fixed ([#24754](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/24754)).
- **Transactions dropped from the mempool now log the reason at warn level** ([#25000](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25000)).

## For wallet / PXE developers

No breaking API changes.

- **Faster sync.** Data fetched from the node is cached and reused instead of re-fetched on every sync ([#24969](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/24969), [#25074](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25074), [#25076](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25076)), and note discovery does less scanning work ([#24275](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/24275), [#25045](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25045), [#24667](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/24667)).
- **Contracts built against the v5.0.1 handshake registry keep working** — the client and release image now ship the historical registry artifacts ([#25032](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25032), [#25155](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25155)).
- **One failing write no longer aborts unrelated writes running alongside it** ([#25208](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25208)).
- **`aztec.js` waits briefly before the first receipt poll after sending a transaction**, removing a round trip that could never succeed ([#25089](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25089)).

## Security & correctness

Everything the node parses from untrusted input now has explicit size bounds, closing memory-exhaustion holes. Most of this lives in shared serialization code, so clients that talk to a node they don't trust get the same protection.

- Tree sibling paths and vectors are bounded ([#25028](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25028)); arrays in the `Tx` and `HashedValues` schemas are capped ([#25029](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25029)); simulation overrides and checkpoint queries on the RPC surface are capped ([#25026](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25026)).
- Gaps in checkpoint block-shape and block-count validation are closed ([#25229](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25229)).
- JSON-RPC responses always include a `result` key, as the spec requires, so an empty result can't be confused with a malformed response ([#24840](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/24840)).

## New in this release

- **Declarative deployments at `@aztec/aztec/deploy`** — describe a deployment as data (contracts, dependencies, bridging, fees) and let the runner work out the order and execute it, instead of hand-written deploy scripts ([#24685](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/24685)).

## Also in this release

- JSON-RPC servers report metrics ([#25159](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25159)), and log levels map to AWS severity ([#25022](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25022)).
- JSON-RPC clients accept and send cookies, so load balancers that use session affinity work ([#25231](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25231)). The RPC server's HTTP timeouts and CORS headers are configurable via `RPC_HTTP_KEEP_ALIVE_TIMEOUT_MS`, `RPC_HTTP_HEADERS_TIMEOUT_MS` and `RPC_CORS_ALLOWED_HEADERS`; defaults are unchanged ([#25242](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25242)).
- Browser: an undersized CRS no longer fails to load ([#24894](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/24894)), and wasm load settings are respected when opening SQLite ([#24937](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/24937)).
- `snappy` is pinned to 7.2.2 and the `aztec-up` local-network wait no longer hangs forever ([#25198](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25198)); bb's socket startup no longer times out while the bb process is alive ([#24802](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/24802)).

## Protocol constants

Unchanged from v5.1.0:

```
vk root               0x2b3b6ea4412b9c8f6457a37f91a2870306f8641e07e16a49b68bda6f8bc02892
protocol contracts    0x2c075866eafc88a1f6f9addc7e337c6e64e45d1cb7fd7c0d612ebcec72aab2ca
```

Protocol circuits and protocol contracts ship as pinned, pre-built artifacts that are byte-identical to v5.1.0's — they are not recompiled, so the Noir compiler upgrade cannot change them. Compatibility tests re-enabled in this release assert both values against the live mainnet and testnet rollups ([#25136](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25136)). This is why the upgrade is drop-in.

## Reference

- [v5.1.0 release notes](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/releases/tag/v5.1.0) — the previous minor release and this release's baseline.
- [v5.0.0 release notes](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/releases/tag/v5.0.0) — the first stable v5 release and full v4→v5 migration reference.
- [Migration notes](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/blob/v5.2.0/docs/docs-developers/docs/resources/migration_notes.md) — per-change migration reference. Note that entries under the "TBD" heading are staged for a future release and do not all apply to v5.2.0; the only breaking change in this release is the one listed above.

NethermindEth/nethermind.name: v2.1.0
NethermindEth/nethermind.body:
# Release notes

359 merged pull requests since 2.0.0, from 29 contributors.

> **Upgrade every Sepolia node to 2.1.0 before the Glamsterdam fork on Tue, 06 Oct 2026, 13:53:36 UTC.** 

For most nodes this is an in-place upgrade with no resync. Read *Breaking changes* first if you run on the **flat** backend with a custom sync config, run **poacore**, run a **Flashbots relay**, parse **Parity-style traces**, or build **plugins** against Nethermind. **

## Highlights

- **Glamsterdam on Sepolia.** Final EIP-8037 state-gas rules, the `TX_MAX_TOTAL_GAS_LIMIT` transaction cap, and Engine API alignment for Amsterdam. (#13140, #13484, #13627, #13554, #13583, #13586, #13755)
- **Faster EVM.** The interpreter loop is replaced by tail-call chain dispatch, stack words stay in `UInt256` limb layout, storage values stay as `UInt256` until they are persisted, and JUMPDEST analysis is rewritten. (#13128, #13323, #13420, #13189, #13810)
- **Lower `engine_newPayload` latency.** The response goes out as soon as the block has executed and its roots match, before the commit. `engine_forkchoiceUpdated` still waits for that head's commit. GC pauses no longer stall payloads the way they did. (#13647, #13711, #13476, #13334)
- **Per-transaction changeset index for flat archives (opt-in).** A single-transaction trace starts at its target transaction instead of replaying the whole block before it: `debug_traceTransaction` went from ~7.1 s to ~28 ms in the PR's measurements. Whole-block traces run their transactions in parallel (6–10× faster). Enable with `FlatDb.HistoryTransactionIndexEnabled=true`. (#13454, #13426)
- **BAL healing after snap sync (flat backend).** On the flat backend, the state left by snap sync is healed by replaying block access lists instead of downloading trie nodes. It is on by default (`Sync.BalHealing=true`); set it to `false` to go back to trie-node healing. snap/2 is advertised only when BAL healing can run. (#12945)
- **Dual-stack IPv4/IPv6 networking.** RLPx, discv4 and discv5 listen on both families, ENRs advertise both, and there is a new `Network.ExternalIpV6` override. (#12679, #12982, #12983, #13731)
- **Flat backend safety rails.** A flat DB that RocksDB had to auto-repair is now re-synced instead of trusted. Unsafe flat activations are refused at start instead of silently corrupting or discarding state. (#13645, #13644)
- **Reclaim the patricia trie after a trie→flat conversion.** `FlatDb.DropPruningTrieState=true` deletes the old trie store on the next start once the flat DB owns the state (~227 GB on mainnet). Off by default. (#13572)
- **RocksDB 11 through Nethermind's own bindings.** The RocksDB package is replaced with `Nethermind.RocksDbBindings` (RocksDB v10 → v11): source-generated P/Invoke with no marshalling stubs, and every native handle held in a `SafeHandle`. (#12853)
- **New EF bootnodes.** The EF bootnode entries for mainnet, Sepolia and Hoodi are replaced with the new NodeOps fleet: five dual-stack nodes running both discv4 and discv5. (#13313)
- **More zkVM targets.** Stateless guests for SP1 and OpenVM ship alongside ZisK, and the ZisK toolchain moves to 1.3.0-alpha. (#13435, #13769, #13743)

## Performance

- **EVM dispatch and call frames:** 3.8–4.5% faster block processing on the superblocks, realblocks and fusaka benchmark sets. (#13189)
- **Storage values held as `UInt256`:** SLOAD 9–18%, SSTORE 42% and TSTORE ~50% faster, with no allocations on those paths. (#13420)
- **EVM stack in limb layout:** 45–53% faster ADD, 16–36% faster SUB, and 9–18% faster shifts. (#13323)
- **JUMPDEST analysis:** worst-case analysis of 64 KiB initcode (a 200 MGas block of PUSH1/JUMPDEST patterns) drops from 0.4–3.2 s to 22–153 ms, depending on the SIMD tier. Initcode is analysed on first use. (#13810)
- **Trie and storage-key hashing:** 35–80% less time on transaction and receipt-root workloads. (#13552)
- **Prewarming:** a single fan-out while senders arrive gives superblocks processing a median −4.4%, P99 −27.9%, and +7.6% MGas/s. Prewarming and trie concurrency caps are removed, and parallel work is budgeted across the state root, blooms, the receipts root and prewarming (2–4% faster processing). (#13640, #13388, #13770)
- **Carried caches:** pre-block account and storage caches are carried across blocks. (#13100)
- **Discovery traffic:** on a warm-started Hoodi node, discovery traffic fell by 90% (152 KiB/s → 15 KiB/s), and the standalone bootnode uses ~44% less working set. (#13122)
- **Snap sync:** downloads are bounded and overlap with response processing. Whale-storage verification in `FlatTrieVerifier` is parallelised. (#12623, #12615)
- **RPC:** `eth_call`, `eth_estimateGas` and `eth_createAccessList` no longer hash the transaction on every run (~0.2 ms on large calldata) (#13804). the stream interpreter is off by default because it lost on every measured `eth_call` shape. `eth_getFilterChanges` is served from shared block logs. (#12999, #13742)
- **Intel hybrid CPUs:** block processing is pinned to the performance cores by default (`Blocks.ProcessingCores`). Nothing changes on other CPUs. (#13717)

## ⚠️ Breaking changes

### If you run a node (config and startup)

- **poacore / poacore_validator now ship `FlatDb.Enabled=false`** because they use FastSync without SnapSync (#13644). A node on those configs that synced on 2.0.0 is on the flat backend, since flat is 2.0.0's default. On 2.1.0 it **refuses to start** (`Refusing --FlatDb.Enabled=false on an existing flat DB`). Either pass `-FlatDb.Enabled=true`, or delete the `flat`, `flatHistory` and `persistedSnapshot` directories and resync the state.
- **`-FlatDb.Enabled=false` on an existing flat DB is refused.** In 2.0.0 the node silently discarded the state and resynced (#13428). It now stops with an error. (#13644)
- **Flat + `Sync.FastSync=true` + `Sync.SnapSync=false` is refused on a fresh node.** Legacy tree sync on the flat backend can leave holes in the state. An already-synced node keeps running and logs a warning. The exception is importing from patricia (`FlatDb.ImportFromPruningTrieState=true` on a datadir that holds patricia state). (#13644)
- **New `FlatDb.OnRepair` setting, default `Resync`.** If RocksDB auto-repairs the flat DB, the node now wipes the flat state and runs state sync again. Headers, bodies and receipts are kept. **Archive nodes synced from genesis cannot snap-resync.** Set `FlatDb.OnRepair=Ignore` and plan a resync yourself if a repair is ever reported. (#13645)
- **`Receipt.MaxBlockDepth` default raised back from 1,000 to 10,000**, and the limit is now also enforced on `eth_getFilterLogs`. On nodes with the log index, only blocks the index cannot serve count towards the limit. A filter created by `eth_newFilter` over a wider range is still accepted, but `eth_getFilterLogs` on it fails with `32602`. (#13131)
- **Removed config keys:** `FlatDb.EnablePreimageRecording`, `Db.PreimageDbRocksDbOptions`, `Db.PreimageDbAdditionalRocksDbOptions` (#13690), `LogIndex.VerifyRpcResponse` (#13131), and `Grpc.Enabled`, `Grpc.Host`, `Grpc.Port` along with the gRPC endpoint (#13330). A JSON config that still sets them logs `Invalid configuration settings` at startup. Remove them from configs, environment variables and command-line flags.
- **`Merge.CompactMemory` default changed from `Yes` to `No`.** This removes GC compaction stalls from `engine_newPayload`. Steady-state RSS may be somewhat higher. (#13476)
- **`Init.LogRules` no longer routes to Seq**, and `Seq.MinLevel` is now the floor for the Seq target. To send a namespace's Trace output to Seq, add an explicit `writeTo="seq"` rule in `NLog.config`. (#13419)
- **Dual-stack by default.** With `Network.LocalIp` unset, the P2P TCP and discovery UDP listeners now try to bind `[::]` on Linux and Windows, so **the P2P port may now be reachable over IPv6**. Check your firewall. macOS stays IPv4-only. Set `Network.LocalIp=0.0.0.0` to keep IPv4-only. (#12982)
- **`Pruning.FullPruningTrigger=VolumeFreeSpace` with a threshold too low to ever trigger now logs a startup warning.** Automatic pruning was already not running in that case, so nothing new is broken. (#13485)

### If you run a Flashbots relay

- **`Flashbots.EnableValidation` now defaults to `true`.** `flashbots_validateBuilderSubmissionV3` checks the submitted block's state root, receipts root, gas used and logs bloom against its execution. Set it to `false` explicitly to get the old behaviour. (#13452)

### If you integrate over JSON-RPC / Engine API

- **`eth_getHeaderByNumber("pending")` returns `null`**, matching go-ethereum and execution-apis#877. (#13082)
- **`proof_getTransactionByHash` / `proof_getTransactionReceipt` return `result: null`** for a transaction they cannot serve, instead of a `32000` error. `proof_getTransactionReceipt` returns `32002` when the block can no longer be retraced. (#13366)
- **Parity `vmTrace` stack pushes are hex quantities** (`0x0`, `0x1`), not byte strings. Word operations now report their pushes. (#13750, #13487)
- **Other trace output changes.** Empty trace selections are accepted. `trace_get` keeps lookup errors instead of replacing them. `trace_filter` returns an error when the requested history is unavailable, and buffered `trace_filter` now applies a single `JsonRpc.Timeout` to the whole request. Deleted-account fields carry deletion markers. `callTracer` omits `to` on a failed top-level CREATE. (#13667, #13676, #13677, #13668, #13078)
- **EIP-3155 / `structLogs` traces are corrected:** `gasUsed` is the top-level execution-gas delta, refunds are cumulative, and opcode names follow Geth (`0x44` is reported as `DIFFICULTY`). (#12981)
- **`eth_estimateGas` runs entirely against the requested block**, the way `eth_call` does, with a single deterministic search. Before, the first run used a synthetic next-block header. Estimates can differ from 2.0.0 within the error margin. Invalid-opcode and stack failures now return the standard error texts (for example `invalid opcode: INVALID`, `stack underflow (0 <=> 2)`), and `eth_call` uses the same texts. (#13899)
- **`eth_call` with `maxPriorityFeePerGas` above `maxFeePerGas`** (after London) fails before any gas is bought, with the same `max priority fee per gas higher than max fee per gas` error execution returns. `eth_createAccessList` fills the fee cap as the priority fee plus twice the base fee when only a priority fee is given. (#13904)
- **Call requests with `gasPrice` and a type-specific field** (`accessList`, `blobVersionedHashes`, `authorizationList`) but no explicit `type` are no longer decoded as legacy transactions. `eth_call`, `eth_estimateGas`, `eth_createAccessList` and `eth_simulateV1` results change for those requests. (#13450)
- **`eth_subscribe("logs")` delivers logs for every block that becomes canonical,** and `removed: true` logs for every block that leaves the canonical chain. A subscriber that falls more than 1,000 blocks behind (or 10,000 events for pending-transaction and peer subscriptions) is disconnected. (#13451)
- **No state for a block now returns `32002` from every method,** and guard-rail rejections (`32002`, `32005`, `4444`) are no longer logged at WARN. (#13643)
- **The SSZ-REST Engine API moves from `/engine/v2/...` to `/engine/v1/...`,** per execution-apis#793. The JSON-RPC `engine_*` surface is unchanged. (#13023)
- **`engine_newPayload` rejects a post-Shanghai payload with a null withdrawals list** (`MissingWithdrawals`). (#13501)
- **`/data/events`** accepts `?events=`. A client that only needs processing statistics should pass `?events=processed`. (#13334)

### If you build against Nethermind (plugin / library authors)

These are source-breaking changes: **rebuild your plugins against 2.1.0.**

- `IBackgroundTaskScheduler.TryScheduleTask` now takes a request type that implements `IBackgroundTaskRequest<TReq>`, and the `source` string is gone. (#9956)
- `ISyncPeerPool.Free` is removed. `SyncPeerAllocation` is now `IDisposable`, so dispose it with `using`. (#13094)
- World-state scopes are opened with `TryBeginScope` / `TryBeginScopeAtTarget`, which return `false` for an unavailable base instead of throwing. (#13522)
- Storage APIs take `UInt256` values instead of byte arrays. `SlotValue` is removed. (#13420)
- EVM extension API: the gas-policy methods are `TryConsume*`, the `OutOfGas` flag is removed, and the `EvmStack` constructors require a `CodeInfo`. (#13189)
- `ProcessingOptions.Trace` is removed. Use `TraceProcessingOptions.ReadOnlyReplay`. (#13443)
- Value-hash and protocol API changes in the txpool and networking code. (#13592)
- Nullable reference types are enabled in EVM, Trie, State and 7 foundation projects. (#13099, #12155)

### Consensus / protocol

- **Glamsterdam (Amsterdam-gated, Sepolia from 10-06):** the EIP-8037 spill is repaid after a child frame merges, and a restored spill is burnt on a top-level halt (#13140, #13484). `TX_MAX_TOTAL_GAS_LIMIT` (2³² − 1) is enforced in the pool, in block validation and in `eth_estimateGas` (#13627). The unknown-original storage flag is kept across repeated writes (#13554). The EL no longer enforces slot ordering on `engine_forkchoiceUpdatedV4` (#13583). Orphaned headers are checked for a slot number (#13586). `engine_getPayloadV5` is rejected from Amsterdam on (#13755).
EIP-7928 receipt event metadata is corrected (#13509), and AuRa keeps existing accounts in BAL preprocessing (#13047).
- **XDC:** randomize-contract transactions now pay and burn gas (#13359), and sign-transaction receipts are encoded as legacy in the receipts trie. The receipts change fixes a consensus divergence on typed transactions (#13375).

## Sync, database & state

- Recovery of missing contract code. (#9417)
- A fast-sync body could be dropped by the block cache, which left the receipts stage stuck. Fixed. **Nodes already stuck on this need a bodies resync.** (#13474)
- Flat persistence keeps going when the committed state is off the canonical chain. `MinReorgDepth` stays reachable after folding to the finalized boundary. Flat state is retained across Engine-X reorgs. (#13591, #13550, #13402)
- A gather whose state was just persisted is retried instead of refused (fixes an occasional `32002 No state available` at the block being folded). (#13763)
- `VerifyWithTrie` no longer reports a false positive when an account is deleted that the trie still holds. (#13521)
- `debug_resetHead` prunes flat snapshots that are unreachable from the new head. (#13524)
- New `FlatDb.EnableCarryForwardCache` (default `true`) to turn off the cross-head read cache. (#13752)
- The history-walk ETA overflow no longer kills progress or discards a finished archive-proof walk (this bug is present in 2.0.0). The walk also reports the replay block of a storage range. (#13761, #13791, #13604, #13754, #13620)
- `SyncServer` range-broadcast serialised. Pooled lists from trie path recovery are disposed. (#12728, #13266)
- `ElapsedMicroseconds` overflow on long-running stopwatches fixed. (#13416)
- The history pruner is created before the block processor starts. (#13285)
- When a block wipes a contract's storage, the pre-block storage cache now invalidates only that contract. Before, it dropped the whole cache and logged an Info line each time, which on pre-Cancun history meant tens of thousands of lines an hour during a full sync from genesis. (#13850)
- The disk-space probe is skipped when the availability check is disabled. (#13456)
